# Authorization

Blacklight has exactly one place that decides what somebody may do:
`authz.Can(ctx, subject, action, resource)`, in `internal/authz`. No handler makes a role
decision — handlers are not given the information to make one. This page is that package's rule
table, rendered.

v1 decided per handler, and every authorization failure in it followed from that: an ungated user
management page, spectators who could write, and two definitions of "blue" that disagreed. The
tables below are the model in full; if a permission is not in them, nobody has it.

## The two levels

| Level | Values | Means |
|---|---|---|
| Platform role | `admin`, `member` | What you may do to this installation. Every account has exactly one. |
| Engagement role | `lead`, `red`, `blue`, `observer` | What you may do inside one engagement. One per engagement you belong to; none if you are not a member. |

They are separate vocabularies on purpose. Being a lead of an engagement confers nothing on the
installation, and being a platform admin is not a seat in anybody's exercise — although an admin
does hold every engagement-scoped action on every engagement, membership or not.

## How to read the tables

- `✓` — holds the action. `·` — does not.
- **Denial is the default.** A combination that is not a `✓` is refused, and refusal says why.
- A refusal that would confirm something the caller may not know — that an engagement exists, that
  an unrevealed step exists — is answered **404**, not 403. The rest are 403.
- The **token scope** column applies only to requests authenticated by a service token. A token
  must hold both the listed scope *and* its owner's live role: revoking or demoting the owner
  constrains the token immediately, with no change to the token.

## Platform actions

Acts on the installation itself. Engagement membership is irrelevant to these.

| Action | admin | member | Token scope | What it covers |
|---|:-:|:-:|---|---|
| `user.read` | ✓ | · | `admin:read` | Read accounts, their platform roles and their status. |
| `user.manage` | ✓ | · | `admin:write` | Invite, edit, disable and delete accounts, and set platform roles. |
| `settings.read` | ✓ | · | `admin:read` | Read platform settings, including how hard this installation is to sign in to. |
| `settings.manage` | ✓ | · | `admin:write` | Change platform settings, including the MFA policy. |
| `activity.read` | ✓ | · | `admin:read` | Read the installation-wide activity log. |
| `content.read` | ✓ | ✓ | `content:read` | Read the shared technique and test-case library. |
| `content.sync` | ✓ | · | `content:sync` | Sync the library from its upstream sources. |
| `content.manage` | ✓ | · | `content:write` | Enable, disable, delete and edit content sources, and author custom content. |
| `engagement.create` | ✓ | ✓ | `engagements:write` | Create an engagement. Acts on the installation, because the engagement does not exist yet. |
| `token.read` | ✓ | ✓ | `admin:read` | List your own service tokens and when they were last used. Never their secrets. |
| `token.manage` | ✓ | ✓ | `admin:write` | Create and revoke your own service tokens. A signed-in session only, never a token itself. |
| `token.admin_read` | ✓ | · | `admin:read` | Read the service tokens one account holds, and when they were last used. Never their secrets. |
| `token.admin_manage` | ✓ | · | `admin:write` | Revoke somebody else's service token. A signed-in session only, never a token itself. |
| `session.read` | ✓ | ✓ | `admin:read` | List the browsers you are signed in on. Never the tokens in their cookies. |
| `session.manage` | ✓ | ✓ | `admin:write` | Revoke your own sessions, one at a time or everywhere but here. A signed-in session only. |

## Engagement actions

Acts on one engagement's contents. The engagement-role columns mean *in that engagement*;
a role held elsewhere grants nothing here. A non-member is refused with a 404.

| Action | platform admin | lead | red | blue | observer | non-member | Token scope | What it covers |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|---|---|
| `engagement.read` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | `engagements:read` | See that an engagement exists and read its settings. |
| `engagement.manage` | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | · | `engagements:write` | Change an engagement's settings, including whether it runs blind. |
| `engagement.delete` | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | · | `engagements:write` | Delete an engagement and everything in it. |
| `member.read` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | `engagements:read` | Read who is in an engagement and in what seat. |
| `member.manage` | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | · | `engagements:write` | Add, remove and re-seat members of one engagement. |
| `execution.read` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | `engagements:read` | Read an execution and its steps. |
| `execution.write_red` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | `engagements:write` | Write the attack side of an execution: what was run, when, and how. |
| `execution.write_blue` | ✓ | ✓ | · | ✓ | · | · | `engagements:write` | Write the detection side of an execution: what was seen, alerted and blocked. |
| `comment.write` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | `engagements:write` | Comment. The one write an observer holds, because reading and commenting is the seat. |
| `finding.write` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | `engagements:write` | Raise and edit findings. |
| `report.read` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | `reports:read` | Read and export an engagement's reports. |
| `report.publish` | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | · | `reports:write` | Publish a report, which is the act that makes it somebody else's evidence. |

## Guards

A guard is an extra condition applied *after* a role grants the action, so a ✓ above can
still be refused for one of these reasons.

- **`session-only`** — Available to a signed-in session and never to a service token, whatever scopes the token carries and whatever its owner may do. It guards the actions that change which credentials exist: a token able to mint another one could outlive its own revocation, which neither the scope fence nor the owner's role would catch.
  Applies to: `token.read`, `token.manage`, `token.admin_read`, `token.admin_manage`, `session.read`, `session.manage`.
- **`blind-mode`** — In a blind engagement, a member in the `blue` seat cannot reach a step that has not been revealed — not even to learn it exists. The same filter is applied in the query layer, so a missing rule still cannot leak one. A platform admin who is *not* a member of the engagement is unaffected; one who has taken the blue seat is held to it.
  Applies to: `execution.read`, `execution.write_blue`.

## Service tokens

A service token is fenced twice. The action must be permitted to the token's **owner**, by the
tables above and their live role at the moment of the request, **and** the token must carry the
scope listed for that action. Neither fence is sufficient on its own, so a token issued while its
holder was an administrator stops being an administrator's token the moment they are demoted.

Scopes are deliberately coarse; the full list is derived from the tables above.

## Where this is enforced

In one middleware, `internal/httpapi/authorize.go`, which is the only caller of `authz.Can` in the
tree — a test fails the build if a second one appears. Each operation in `api/openapi.yaml` names the
action it needs (`x-authz-action`), or carries a written exemption; an operation that names neither
is a server that refuses to start. See [`docs/api.md`](api.md#authorization) for the mapping and
[`docs/http.md`](http.md#authorization) for what a refusal looks like on the wire.

## Changing this model

Edit the rule table in `internal/authz/policy.go` and run `make generate`. Everything else follows:

- Adding an `Action` without a rule fails the exhaustiveness test — silence is not a permission.
- The permission matrix (`internal/authz/matrix_test.go`) fails until somebody writes down, by hand,
  what every role may do with the new action. It enumerates the actions from the same enum but states
  the answers independently — a matrix that computed them the way `Can` does would agree with a bug.
- Role names exist only in `internal/authz`. A role string anywhere else in the Go tree fails a test,
  which is the direct fix for v1's two contradictory definitions of "blue".
